core.text: Host: the existing Endless Museum. Keep museum encounters, tutorial learning and critical-poetic writing as overlapping sets. Teach selected reusable operations; name supplied support. Keep decisions, proposals, evidence and unknowns distinct. Preserve why a choice was made. Move project → sequence → hall → source → sequence → project. Current writing scope: summaries; do not alter museum code, hall order or full lessons to make a summary true. The memory interface is a tool for this work.
core.reason: Repeated local rewrites lost the museum setting and prior author decisions. Compact instructions should preserve intent and support changes without flattening artistic differences.
core.open_question: Which sequence boundary should receive the next deliberate reading? Preserve mature sequences unless evidence gives a reason to reopen them.

sequence:primitives.summary: Arrival → represented point → coordinates → relation → retained list → grid address → face → connected faces → generated form → limit → composition.
sequence:primitives.reason: A usable material travels onward. The closing halls can reflect and compose rather than introduce more syntax.
sequence:primitives.open_question: Where should each reduced learner construction run inside the existing museum?

map:Point_Line_Grid.summary: Fit the accepted drawing, then round display positions. Keep source data separate.
map:Point_Line_Grid.reason: This is the concrete return from a recorded list to lattice addresses; it also constrains the later Array analogy.
map:Point_Line_Grid.open_question: How should the lesson make source position and displayed address visible without overloading the learner?

findings.text: Keep the lineage open to change. Show the current order and complete summaries together, while preserving alternatives, reasons and open questions. A hall may contribute through reflection or an encounter without introducing a new programming step.
findings.reason: Palle approved the continuous outline on 4 October 2026 with the instruction: “keep the freedom of change.” The interface should support reconsideration as the project evolves.
findings.sequence_effect: Compare neighbouring halls and question their order or teaching selection without silently rewriting the authored route.
findings.project_effect: Keep museum, tutorial and critical writing as overlapping sets. A memory structure is an aid to judgment, not a fixed curriculum.
findings.method: Explicit author instruction in this conversation, 4 October 2026; a design decision, not a source or runtime observation.
findings.review_note: Retained as an explicit author instruction for the memory interface. This records the requested freedom to reconsider choices; it makes no runtime or whole-curriculum claim.
